sentences.text: Bavaricarbo is an extinct genus of cormorant that lived in the Miocene of Germany.
The type species of the genus is B. brevirostris.
The fossils were recovered from the Hammerschmiede clay pit in southern Germany.
Bavaricarbo was first described by Mayr, Lechner, and Böhme in a paper published in the Swiss Journal of Palaeontology.
The species lived during the Miocene epoch.
The coexistence of Bavaricarbo with other fish-eating birds indicates that the Hammerschmiede locality supported a highly productive river system rich in prey.
It is placed in the stem group of the cormorant family Phalacrocoracidae.
Fossils date to the early Late Miocene, specifically the earliest Tortonian, from the Hammerschmiede clay pit in southern Germany.
